classification.difficultyReason: Track vertices through two rotations on the supplied angular grid, then combine their directed angles, distinguishing addition from cancellation when directions differ.

content.prompt: Perform each pair of rotations on the given figure. Then find a single rotation that has the same effect. All rotations are about $O$.

spec.description: Square polar drawing scaffold with six concentric circles and rays at 30-degree intervals. Original triangle is blue and centre O is red.
spec.mathematics: Using one circle spacing as a drawing unit, A=(90 degrees,2), B=(120 degrees,5), C=(90 degrees,5) in polar coordinates about O. These coordinates are construction specifications, not printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original triangle and polar scaffold are visible.

answer.worked:
Rotate each vertex one $30^\circ$ division anticlockwise and join the images to form $A'B'C'$. Rotate these vertices two more divisions anticlockwise to form $A''B''C''$. Keep each vertex on its original circle.

The rotations have the same direction, so their angles add:
$$30^\circ+60^\circ=90^\circ.$$
The equivalent rotation is $90^\circ$ anticlockwise about $O$.

spec.description: Square polar drawing scaffold with six concentric circles and rays at 30-degree intervals. Original triangle is blue and centre O is red.
spec.mathematics: Using one circle spacing as a drawing unit, A=(150 degrees,2), B=(150 degrees,6), C=(120 degrees,4) in polar coordinates about O. These coordinates are construction specifications, not printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original triangle and polar scaffold are visible.

answer.worked:
Rotate each vertex one $30^\circ$ division anticlockwise and join the images to form $A'B'C'$. Rotate these vertices two divisions clockwise to form $A''B''C''$. Keep each vertex on its original circle.

The clockwise rotation exceeds the anticlockwise rotation by
$$60^\circ-30^\circ=30^\circ.$$
The equivalent rotation is $30^\circ$ clockwise about $O$.
